evidence: Final normal-scale labeled direction-sheet.png and focused head crops, plus three independent blind axis reviews.

directions.observed: Raised chin and open face, original eyes directed upward.
directions.reason: Chin extends above collar; face is pitched back and eye line is raised. Body and feet remain frontal.

directions.observed: Raised face with gentle screen-right yaw.
directions.reason: Face projects right of head center; visible right-side profile and raised chin distinguish it from neutral and pure up.

directions.observed: Upward screen-right gaze and head turn.
directions.reason: Rightward cheek projection and raised eye line are visible with torso and apron held frontal.

directions.observed: Stronger right turn with upward pitch.
directions.reason: Near eye dominates and far eye is partly hidden under fringe, with chin lifted relative to 112.5.
Nose and cheek point right; far eye is occluded. Feet and apron remain forward, so this is a head turn.
Crown becomes more exposed and eye line drops beneath fringe while cheek and visible eye remain right of center.

directions.observed: Deep downward pitch with slight right yaw.
directions.reason: Lowered eye line and tucked chin are clear; asymmetric fringe and cheek retain a rightward bias confirmed by all blind reviewers.

directions.observed: Downward gaze approaching frontal; horizontal component is difficult to read at normal scale.
directions.reason: Crown and lowered eyes establish down. Both eyes nearly symmetric; the intended small right component is ambiguous to all blind reviewers. Accepted as a near-vertical transition, not as a strong right cue.
Symmetric crown and fringe dominate above the lowered face; chin is tucked close to collar. Both blind vertical cardinal checks passed.

directions.observed: Downward face with a slight left offset.
directions.reason: Eye line remains low; cheek projects left beneath the fringe. All three blind reviewers found leftward bias.
Left cheek and near eye dominate below a visible crown; nose projects left while apron and feet stay frontal.

directions.observed: Clear left turn with lowered chin.
directions.reason: Far eye is obscured and left-facing cheek projects out; chin lies lower than in 292.5.
Visible eye, nose and cheek face left while body remains forward. All three blind horizontal cardinal reviews passed.
Chin and eye line rise; far eye is hidden and cheek projects left, unlike the corresponding down-left pose.
Raised face and left-offset nose/cheek remain readable without relying on labels; all blind reviewers agree.

directions.observed: Raised nearly frontal face; horizontal component is difficult to read at normal scale.
directions.reason: Chin and eyes clearly point up. Both eyes appear almost symmetric; all blind reviewers marked the intended slight left component ambiguous. Accepted as the transition back to pure up.

continuity_review.alpha_holes: Flagged low rows are the expected transparent gap between separated legs below the skirt, not missing material in head or clothing.
continuity_review.157.5_to_180: Reviewed normal-scale boundary. Approximately 11 percent visible-area change and 3.8px center movement; small size step, no detached features or character identity change.
continuity_review.337.5_to_000: Reviewed wrap boundary. Approximately 6.8 percent visible-area change and 4.7px center movement; head pitch stays upward and body stays planted.
continuity_review.limitations: Several neighboring up-right poses are similar. Near-vertical horizontal cues at 157.5 and 337.5 remain subtle/ambiguous. No cardinal ambiguity or opposite-direction error was observed.
